### Independent Projects & R&D

Recent independent work spans industrial LLM systems, application security, and geospatial machine learning, alongside open-source developer tools. Projects include private products and self-hosted tooling for Russian-language and regulated technical domains.

#### Dali (ДаЛи) — on-prem RCA diagnostics for industrial equipment
- **Status:** MVP in progress; the service stack is deployed and running.
- Root-cause analysis of equipment failures from a symptom description. Produces a structured RCA report: root causes with evidence citations, an Ishikawa / 5-Why breakdown, and recommended actions, built on a RAG pipeline. Russian language; all data stays inside the partner's network. First pilot runs on an assembly line.
- Built the system as composable services: an OpenAI-compatible RCA engine, a Chainlit UI for engineers, an admin UI for content, prompts and evaluation, an input guard, and a native retrieval store.
- Split out **dali-drawing**, a standalone service that turns engineering drawings (PDF) into structured records. A vector branch (PyMuPDF) handles born-digital CAD files; an OCR branch (RapidOCR on ONNX Runtime) handles scans; an LLM fills in the GOST title-block fields. Isolated to keep the heavy computer-vision dependencies separate and give it its own release cycle, shipped through GHCR CI/CD.
- *Technologies and methods:*
  - **Backend & UI:** Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Chainlit, Jinja2, HTMX; OpenAI-compatible APIs and SSE streaming.
  - **LLM pipelines:** Haystack ingestion and retrieval/reasoning pipelines, LiteLLM for provider routing, DeepSeek, Ollama with local bge-m3 embeddings; vision-language models for drawing and symptom-photo interpretation.
  - **Retrieval:** PostgreSQL + pgvector, ParadeDB `pg_search` (BM25), Russian/English full-text search, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), equipment-scoped metadata filtering, and hypothetical-question enrichment (HyQ).
  - **Document processing:** Docling for table-rich PDFs, openpyxl for Excel, PyMuPDF for engineering drawings, RapidOCR + ONNX Runtime for scanned drawings; content-based ingestion routing and structured chunk metadata.
  - **Persistence & access:** psycopg, asyncpg, SQLAlchemy; durable PostgreSQL job queues (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, retries, dead-letter queue and replay), MinIO/S3 with presigned URLs, role-based access and bcrypt password hashing.
  - **Delivery & quality:** Docker Compose, Caddy/TLS, GHCR CI/CD, YAML-managed prompts and runtime settings, unit/E2E tests and RCA evaluation with A/B regression gates.

#### Rubezh (Рубеж) — self-hostable LLM guardrail for the Russian / technical domain
- Built a standalone input guard for prompt injection, jailbreaks, secret exfiltration, and harmful requests, with a Russian technical-domain rubric designed to reduce false positives on legitimate safety-manual vocabulary (explosion, burn, high pressure).
- Implemented interchangeable rules, LLM-as-judge, distilled-classifier, and hybrid backends behind a shared verdict contract and an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` API. The hybrid rejects explicit attacks with rules and escalates remaining input to a model; a dependency-free Python client lets applications choose how to handle unavailable backends.
- Distilled a Qwen2.5-72B teacher into Qwen3-0.6B using LoRA and 4-bit QLoRA on a local RTX A2000 with 4 GB VRAM. Built a synthetic-data pipeline with separate generation and teacher-labeling stages, obfuscation augmentation, deduplication, and held-out benchmark exclusion.
- Added script-aware normalization of leetspeak and homoglyphs before classification, preserving technical numbers and reducing false positives on obfuscated benign text. Evaluated feature and data changes against curated and synthetic red-team sets, including a benchmark labeled by agreement between Qwen2.5-72B and Llama-3.3-70B.
- Measured approximately 87.5–87.9% accuracy on the cleaned synthetic benchmark; human-labeled evaluation remains pending. The distilled model is trained and evaluated locally; production student serving, Dali integration, and output screening remain planned.
- *Technologies and methods:*
  - **Service:** Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, Docker, OpenAI-compatible HTTP API.
  - **Model training:** PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT, TRL, Datasets, Accelerate, bitsandbytes; teacher–student distillation, LoRA/QLoRA, NF4 quantization and gradient checkpointing.
  - **Quality:** pytest, HTTPX, ruff, red-team evaluation, a zero-false-positive CI gate on curated diagnostic cases, and deterministic text normalization.

#### Mushrooms — satellite-based mushroom habitat mapping (private project)
- Built a geospatial ML pipeline for a mushroom-foraging web map of the Leningrad region, combining seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery, Copernicus elevation data, ESA WorldCover forest masks, and weak OpenStreetMap forest-type labels.
- Trained Random Forest classifiers to distinguish coniferous from deciduous forest. Used spatially blocked validation to reduce leakage between nearby training and test samples; achieved approximately 88% agreement with held-out OpenStreetMap labels. Field validation remains pending.
- Used feature ablation and permutation importance to select eight optical and terrain features; removed radar inputs after measuring their limited additional benefit. Produced a region-wide conifer-probability layer at 20-metre resolution, with Google Earth Engine batch processing and local model evaluation.
- Delivered the layer to the web map as PMTiles through Cloudflare R2 and a Worker using HTTP range requests; reduced the tile archive from 466 MiB to 221 MiB through transparency quantization and image compression.
  - *Technologies:* Python, Google Earth Engine, scikit-learn, rasterio, Shapely, mercantile, PMTiles, Pillow, OpenStreetMap/Overpass, osmtogeojson, mapshaper, Cloudflare Workers and R2.

#### Open source
- **[Supportal](https://github.com/Neanderthal/Supportal)** — embeddable relay that connects a website chat widget to a support team working inside a Telegram group, one topic per ticket. FastAPI + aiogram, SQLite or PostgreSQL.
- **[map-vectorize](https://github.com/Neanderthal/map-vectorize)** — automatic vectorization of raster geological maps (GGK-1000/3) into GeoJSON: georeferencing plus color segmentation of legend units.
- **[mcp-qemu-vm](https://github.com/Neanderthal/mcp-qemu-vm)** — MCP server that controls QEMU virtual machines, giving an AI agent full computer access inside a disposable sandbox.
- **[unix-pass-mcp](https://github.com/Neanderthal/unix-pass-mcp)** — MCP server exposing the Unix `pass` password manager to MCP clients: read-only by default, gated writes, headless gpg-agent unlock.
- **[security-audit](https://github.com/Neanderthal/security-audit)** — workstation security scanner that checks installed packages for known CVEs via OSV.dev, pip-audit, and cargo-audit.
